_note: Maine fee rules, retrieved verbatim from the Maine Legislature statute site (legislature.maine.gov) on 2026-06-20. 14 M.R.S. §6028 (late-payment penalty: rent is not late until 15 days past due, and the penalty may not exceed 4% of one month's rent, and only if disclosed in writing at signing) and §6022-A (at the start of a tenancy a landlord may not require more than first month's rent + a security deposit capped by §6032 + a properly disclosed mandatory recurring fee). ALL rules status=draft-unverified: review by a Maine tenant attorney / Pine Tree Legal before publishing conclusions.

rules.title: Late fee exceeds 4% of one month's rent
rules.description: Per 14 M.R.S. §6028(2), a landlord may not assess a late-payment penalty that exceeds 4% of the amount due for one month. A late fee stated as a percentage above 4% is unenforceable to that extent. A flat-dollar late fee or a per-day penalty can also exceed the cap, but whether it does depends on the monthly rent, so those are flagged for review rather than asserted illegal.
rules.tenant_explainer: Maine caps the late fee at 4% of one month's rent. A late fee set higher than 4% isn't allowed. A flat dollar amount or a daily charge might also break the cap depending on your rent — worth checking the math.

citations.label: 14 M.R.S. §6028(2) (Maximum penalty)
citations.quote: A landlord may not assess a penalty for the late payment of rent which exceeds 4% of the amount due for one month.

rules.title: Late fee charged before the 15-day grace period
rules.description: Per 14 M.R.S. §6028(1), rent is not 'late' until 15 days past its due date, and §6028(3) requires the late penalty to have been disclosed in writing at signing. A clause imposing a late fee the moment rent is one day (or fewer than 15 days) past due is unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: In Maine your rent isn't legally 'late' until 15 days after it's due, so a landlord can't charge a late fee on day one — and they can only charge one at all if it was spelled out in writing when you signed.

citations.label: 14 M.R.S. §6028(1) (Late payment)
citations.quote: A payment of rent is late if it is not made within 15 days from the time the payment is due.

citations.label: 14 M.R.S. §6028(3) (Notice in writing)
citations.quote: A landlord may not assess a penalty for the late payment of rent unless the landlord gave the tenant written notice at the time they entered into the rental agreement that a penalty, up to 4% of one month's rent, may be charged for the late payment of rent.

rules.title: Up-front charges beyond first month's rent and the lawful deposit
rules.description: Per 14 M.R.S. §6022-A, when a tenancy begins a landlord may not require an initial payment exceeding the first full month's rent, a security deposit capped by §6032, and any properly disclosed mandatory recurring fee. A separate up-front charge labeled 'move-in fee', 'last month's rent' on top of those, 'redecorating fee', or similar is suspect. Flag to check the purpose and total.
rules.tenant_explainer: At move-in, the most a Maine landlord can require up front is your first month's rent, the security deposit (capped at two months), and any properly disclosed recurring fee. An extra move-in charge, redecorating fee, or 'last month's rent' stacked on top probably isn't allowed — check the total.

citations.label: 14 M.R.S. §6022-A(1) (Limit on amount required to initiate tenancy)
citations.quote: Upon entering a lease or tenancy at will agreement, a landlord, landlord's agent or real estate broker may not require a tenant to pay an initial amount of money in excess of the total of the rent for the first full month of occupancy, a security deposit as limited by section 6032 and any mandatory recurring fee as defined in section 6000, subsection 1-A that is properly disclosed under section 6030-J.
